definition: An AI computer sold and engineered as a whole rack (compute trays, switch trays, power shelves, cabling and liquid cooling) rather than as individual servers, so that dozens of accelerators behave like one machine. NVIDIA's NVL72, AMD's Helios and AWS's UltraServers are examples.
NVIDIA's standard GPU baseboard (typically eight GPUs plus NVLink switches) that server makers such as Dell, HPE, Supermicro and Lenovo build their own servers around. HGX-1 (2017) set the pattern.
NVIDIA's own branded AI system (DGX-1 in 2016, later DGX-2, DGX A100, DGX H100 and DGX rack systems), sold directly and through partners; it doubles as NVIDIA's reference design.
The pump-and-heat-exchanger unit that circulates liquid coolant to cold plates in a rack and passes the heat to the building's water loop. One CDU serves one or several racks.
A metal block with internal channels that sits directly on a GPU or CPU; liquid flowing through it carries heat away (direct-to-chip liquid cooling).

An industry foundation, started by Facebook (Meta) in 2011, where hyperscalers and vendors publish open hardware designs for servers, racks and power. NVIDIA contributed its GB200 NVL72 rack design; AMD's Helios uses an OCP rack.
A double-width OCP rack specification for very heavy, high-power AI racks; AMD's Helios is built on it.
A vendor name for a multi-rack AI system sold as one unit: NVIDIA's DGX SuperPOD (for example eight GB200 NVL72 racks) or Huawei's Atlas SuperPoD (thousands of Ascend chips in one scale-up domain).
A contract manufacturer that builds electronics to another company's design (for example Sanmina, Celestica, Foxconn). In AI servers EMS firms and ODMs assemble and test racks at thin margins.
The engineering phase where a new design is turned into a manufacturable, tested product on a factory line; for AI racks this includes thermal, power and cable validation before volume ramp.

A power-electronics converter (built from SiC or GaN switches) that replaces a bulky copper-and-iron transformer, converting medium-voltage grid power directly to the 800 V DC used by next-generation AI racks.
A complete, documented design that a platform owner publishes so partners can build compatible products quickly (NVIDIA's HGX, MGX and DGX SuperPOD architectures are reference designs).
NVIDIA's term for a datacenter built and run mainly to produce AI tokens, designed as one system from power and cooling to racks, networking and software.
A physics-accurate software model of a datacenter (power, cooling, airflow, racks) used to design and test it before construction; NVIDIA's Omniverse DSX blueprint is one.
